name: NAIRA NIWAS · one building, one window a post
one_line: The season told as one blush Bombay-Deco co-op building, three bays wide and four storeys tall, the exact shape of the 3 x 4 profile grid: every post is a reel or a moving carousel that finds its window, opens it and lights it on one true moment of present-day housing-society life with one real Naira piece inside, and the twelve covers, posted in order, assemble on the profile into the building itself, lit from the shops at street level to a wedding on the terrace.
big_idea:
Every woman this feed is for has stood on her balcony in Diwali week and looked across at the building opposite: a kandil in every window, a different light in every flat. This season Naira is that building. It is drawn once, in Naira blush and in the Bombay-Deco manner of Dadar, Matunga and Shivaji Park (speed-line pilasters, eyebrow sunshades, sunburst grilles, a stepped crown): shops at street level, two floors of flats, a terrace on top. Twelve bays, twelve posts, the exact shape of the 3 x 4 grid. Storeys are weeks (week 1 the shops, week 2 the first floor, week 3 the second floor, week 4 the terrace), so on the profile the building is lit from the street up as the season moves from Karwa Chauth to the first muhurat.

Each post opens one bay and lights it. Shop 1's shutter goes up on a tent card that says BACK IN 5 MINUTES (it was eleven weeks). The bangle shop next door is busy the night before Karwa Chauth and the cuff needs no soap. Four blush boxes wait at the gate and the watchman isn't telling who they are for. In 103 the window seat is still disputed. In 102 the brass nameplate gets its tamarind and lemon. On 101's balcony one bulb of the ladi is always out. In 203 she said kahi nako and he believed her. In 202 a chit asks to borrow one of two necklaces. By the lift a notice says LOST: ONE EARRING. On the terrace the cousins have rehearsed for three weeks, the moon comes back with nobody fasting, and on the last Sunday the whole building gets its wedding lights.

The motion is the idea at two scales. Every reel opens on the whole building at exactly one third scale, which IS the profile grid: the season so far lit, the coming weeks dark with unlit kandils. The camera finds this week's window, it opens, the light comes on, the piece is drawn until the light finds it (its traced outline develops into the real photograph), one line lands, and the camera pulls back to a building with one more window lit. Followers watch it fill for four weeks; a visitor sees it finished. On the grid each tile is a whole bay and a complete picture, but every bay shares the same pilasters, string courses, a blush kandil at the same spot and a brass plate at the same spot, so posted in order they become one building standing on the live LAC row.

The emblem is the Naira kandil, an akash kandil in Naira blush with the I-flower cut into one facet, turning once every 10 s (the owner's own number for the flower), true for every date because Maharashtrian kandils stay up until Tripurari Purnima on 24 Nov. The address is the brass plate under every window carrying the real wordmark. The building is drawn; the life inside it is photographed; the jewellery is always the real listing photograph at a stated true scale. The residents recur without ever showing a face (101 Aai, 103 the siblings, 202 the evening-walk friend, 203 the spare-key neighbour), bulb 9 on 101's balcony stays out to the finale, and a soft brass lift-bell rings as each week's kandil lights, so the series is recognisable with the screen off. A stranger names it in three seconds: a pink building at Diwali, and every post lights one window.
how_it_beats_A_and_B:
MOTION IS THE IDEA, AT BOTH LEVELS. All 12 posts move (6 reels, 6 carousels whose slide 1 is a native-action loop), against A's 2 reels and 10 stills and B's 3 reels. Every reel opens on the profile itself and lights one window, so reach turns into profile visits, and P12's pull-back frame is the finished profile.

THE GRID IS ONE PICTURE. Twelve bays form one Deco building on the LAC pavement of the live row; storeys darken from lit shops to wedding night; the terrace row shares one sky and one string-light wire; the real wordmark sits on Shop 1's fascia at bottom-right and on the crown at top-left, on the long diagonal. A is a shade card and B a poster wall: neither composes the profile as one image.

NEWER WIT, SAME HONESTY. Present-day co-op society life (the watchman, the notice by the lift, the spare-key neighbour, kahi nako, the borrowed necklace, the dead bulb) is ground neither A (the matching counter) nor B (Mummy's house) touches. Every joke is a listing truth: the cuff opens across 2.5 cm, the droplet's two ends never meet, the set is sold as two, the huggie closes on a hinged snap, the huggies are brushed not mirror, the Heartbead is cool with warmth only at the front, the Fine Tennis is 'the everyday line of light'.

IT SELLS LIKE A. The exact BUY line is in 11 of 12 captions, nine posts carry a basket (four gifts, a two-metal pair, a stack, the two-necklace set, two mismatched pairs, the three-piece set), the service line (blush box, free insured shipping, COD) closes all twelve end cards and first comments, the gift guide lands Sun 1 Nov at noon, the Bhaubeej hint goes 8 days early, and the top-left tile is a BUY3 set.

IT RE-SKINS NEITHER. Karwa Chauth goes to the bangle shop, not the moon (A and B both use the moon); the four-colour huggie row (A P7) and the neckline guide (A P9) are cut; the kandil is the emblem, never A's 'stays up all month' joke; the finale is the green set while A and B close on Ruby (12 in stock).

IT IS THE SAFER BUILD, NOW PROVEN AGAINST THE ASSETS. One C-WORLD file, twelve bay components with three states, a kandil computed as a true projected bipyramid (no CSS 3D sorting), a box drawn as a fixed 2D projection (no three.js, no face sorting), lights drawn as dotted strokes, 18 AI plates of props and textures only, and every piece checked against its real cut-out: P6 moves to the Fine Tennis Bracelet because the Riviere Eternal has no full-length photograph, P12's three pieces share one true scale, P8 hangs the clean V cut-out from the mirror so its cut ends are hidden, and P11 uses a studio recut of the Heartbead rather than the AI-styled one.
motion_language:
HOUSE PACE (owner-tuned). The slowest thing on screen sets the tempo: the kandil turns once every 10.0 s and sways +-1.2 deg every 5.0 s (5.0 s, not 6.4 s, so it divides every 10 s loop). Camera moves 1.6-2.0 s for a 3x zoom; openings 1.0-2.2 s (the box drawer opens in 1.1 s and closes in 1.0 s, the site's REVEAL figures); lights-on 0.8-1.2 s; type 0.6 s. No shot under 1.5 s, every headline held >= 2.0 s, every end card held >= 2.6 s. Nothing fast, nothing jittery, no flash frames, no camera shake, no spin-for-fun, one overshoot maximum. Tube-light blinks happen once in the season (P1).

EASING. Entrances (type, glows, sparkles, the drawer): cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1), the site's reveal curve; type rises 16 px from opacity 0. Camera and openings (shutter, louvres, doors, curtain, lift gate): cubic-bezier(.65,0,.35,1) (= --ease-inout in kit/motion/motion.css). Constant motion (kandil, sway, fan, wisps, breathing bulbs): sinusoidal or linear. Nothing starts from scale 0 (0.96 minimum).

THE SEVEN MOVES (the whole vocabulary). (1) ESTABLISHING: C-WORLD at scale 0.331492 fills 1080x1920 = the profile grid; posted bays lit, this week's kandil lights with the lift-bell (P1 0.25 s, all others 0.2 s); coming bays dark, kandils unlit and swaying. P1 holds 0.8 s; P4 onwards 0.6 s (P12 1.0 s for the dressing-up). (2) THE FIND: exponential zoom to the bay (scale 1.0) in 1.8 s on P1, 1.6 s from P4 (formula in C-CAMERA). (3) THE OPENING, one per storey: shutter rolls up (P1) / glazed doors swing (P6) / louvred shutters swing (P4) / voile curtain draws (P7) / string lights come on (P10, P12). (4) LIGHTS ON: dark overlay to 0 and a warm bloom from the source, 0.8-1.0 s, warm spill on the plaster round the opening. (5) DRAWN UNTIL THE LIGHT FINDS IT (graft from DRAWN FROM LIFE): in the dark the piece is its own traced outline (C-OUTLINE, cream #F6EFE6 3 px in dark rooms, sage deep #3F5A4C in lit rooms), drawn at about 900 px/s; at lights-on the photograph develops in exactly that footprint (opacity 0-1, blur 6-0 px, scale 1.035-1, 0.9 s, cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1)) while the outline retracts from both ends (0.7 s), overlapping >= 0.4 s. (6) THE GLINT: one light band across the piece masked to its alpha (kit .glint, 1.1 s) and at most three four-point sparkles; once per post except where light is the joke (P5, P6, P11). (7) THE PULL-BACK and THE PLATE: back to establishing scale in 1.8-2.2 s with one more window lit, a 0.3-0.4 s hold, then the end card (C-ENDCARD) dissolves in over 0.5 s, holds >= 2.6 s with only the wordmark's flower turning on the I's stem at 36 deg/s, and dissolves into frame 0 in its last 0.5 s.

LOOP LOGIC (graft from GALLI). Reels: the end card's last 0.5 s dissolves into frame 0 (the establishing building), an honest soft seam. Carousel video slides: frame 0 is the cover and the last frame is pixel-identical to it; every ambient period divides the loop (any loop that contains the kandil is exactly 10.0 s: torsion 10.0, sway 5.0, string-light breathing 5.0, fan 10.0, hung paper 5.0); no cross-fade loops (state changes return by a reverse wipe or a reverse move). Every slide 1 carries a native action, not only a sweep: P2 the soap dish slides to the cuff and back; P3 a draught through the gate flutters the tags and the ledger page; P5 the reflection from the window opposite crosses the nameplate (mirror flash) and the huggies (satin sheen); P8 the chit lifts out of its tuck and settles; P9 the lift gate concertinas open and shut; P11 a wisp clears and moonlight runs bead by bead.

WHAT NEVER MOVES. The jewellery's form: never warped, mirrored, recoloured, spun or scaled on its own (the camera scales it, it may ride a drawer, or hang and swing as a real earring card does; no glass reflections that would mirror it). The wordmark's letters (only its flower turns, on its stem, on end cards). Prices, facts and plates (they fade in and hold). The building's geometry. Type never types on, bounces, scales or tracks.

LIGHT. Warm only (2700 K look); glints ivory #FFF7E6 on gold tone, neutral #F4F2F0 on rhodium; the kandil's flower is the only patterned light; no lens flares, confetti, fireworks or fake bokeh. DEPTH. Foreground architecture moves 1.15x the interior during camera moves (parallax); far things in a room carry 1-1.5 px blur; every cut-out gets a contact-shadow ellipse (multiply 30-38%) plus kit .cut.

SOUND. One instrumental per reel from Instagram's in-app library (no lyrics, no vocals), ducking 4 dB under foley. Baked into every reel: the series signature (a single soft brass lift-bell 'ding', one stroke, about 1.2 s decay, as this week's kandil lights; graft from THE BOX THEATRE's bells) over 1.2 s of building ambience (evening birds, a far scooter, street hum), then 2-4 timed foley hits per post. Carousel slide-1 loops carry 2-3 very soft baked foley hits; an in-app instrumental is optional.

RENDER. Reels: node tools/reel.cjs page.html <s> out.mp4 (30 fps, H.264 High, +faststart); every CSS animation is seeked per frame, and the camera, kandil, box drawer and strands run in window.atTime(ms). Carousel loops: tools/loop.cjs, a copy of reel.cjs with viewport {width:1080,height:1440} (one-line change), or render at 1080x1920 and crop with ffmpeg crop=1080:1440:0:240. Covers and stills: tools/render.cjs + tools/export.py. Pull frames at every key beat (ffmpeg -ss t -frames:v 1) and view them before shipping.

system.type_system:

VELISTA 400 (kit/fonts/Velista.woff2), CAPS ONLY, tracking .03em, line-height .98. Verified glyph set: A-Z, 0-9, . , : ; ' & - ( ) ! ? and È/É (so RIVIÈRE may be Velista); it has NO rupee sign, NO middot, NO degree sign: prices, middots and 'N°' are always Jost. Cover headlines 86-150 px (>= 90 px wherever the words must read in the grid; measured widths are given per post from the font's own advances), signs and boards 72-104 px, label-only plates 52 px.
CORMORANT GARAMOND ITALIC 400, lowercase, 40-56 px: one turn per frame, ending in a full stop; also the chit, the ledger entries and the tag backs (no handwriting font anywhere: no Kalam).

HIERARCHY PER COVER: one Velista headline (or an object that is the headline: P1's tent card, P9's notice, P3's gate), at most one Cormorant turn, the plate, at most one Devanagari line. No type in the top-right 173 x 202 of any tile. On reels, in-frame words stay inside x 72-1008 and y 290-1630 of the 1080x1920 frame and clear of x >= 960 between y 1100-1700.
NAMES IN TYPE: the word NAIRA is never set in type on any image; the brand appears only as the kit wordmark. 'Naira Niwas' is not on any image (caption-only, pending the owner). The URL 'nairaflore.com' is the only typed form of the name, on end cards.
system.emblem:
C-KANDIL, the Naira akash kandil, on all 12 covers at the same place: hung on a 1.5 px gold #C99A4C thread at tile x 140 (from the eyebrow's underside at y 126 on flats, from the fascia's left bracket at y 268 on the shops, from the gate arch's bracket at y 300 on P3, from the far string-light wire at y 205 on P10-P11, from a brass bracket under the crown at y 260 on P12). Body 140 x 190 px (x 70-210), eleven paper tails 6-9 px wide and 150-220 px long below it (alternating #FFBDA8 / #FBF3EC, V-cut tips), a 10 px gold waist band, a small gold cone cap. In the grid it is a 50 x 150 px pink lantern top-left of every tile.
BUILD (redesigned for a true turn, not a breathing width-swap): an SVG hexagonal bipyramid computed per frame in window.atTime(ms) (work/v3/kit/kandil.js). theta = 2*PI*ms/10000 (one full turn per 10.0 s). Equator vertices i = 0..5: phi_i = theta + i*60deg; x_i = 70*sin(phi_i); y_i = 95 + 9*cos(phi_i) (we see it from slightly below). Upper facet i = triangle(apex (0,0), v_i, v_i+1); lower facet = triangle(v_i, v_i+1, apex (0,190)). Draw a facet only if cos(phi_i + 30deg) > 0 (front-facing); fill = mix(shade, key, 0.55 + 0.45*max(0, cos(phi_i + 30deg - (-35deg)))) with the key light 35 deg to the left; lower facets 6% darker. Waist band = the front equator polyline, stroke #C99A4C 10 px. The flower window sits on upper facet 0: a 60 px circle at 58% of the way from apex to the facet's equator edge, scaled horizontally by cos(phi_0 + 30deg), holding kit/naira-flower.svg (52 px tall, fill #FFF1E0), hidden when cos < 0.05. LIT: a 300 px radial halo #FFD9B8 40% -> 0 (screen) behind it, and the flower's light on the plaster beside it as a ghost: kit/naira-flower.svg at 200 px, #FFF1E0, opacity 0.14 * max(0, cos(phi_0 + 30deg)), blur 6 px, screen, x offset 80*sin(phi_0 + 30deg) (inside the brand's 6-15% ghost rule). SWAY: rotate(1.2deg * sin(2*PI*ms/5000)) about the thread top; each tail adds its own rotate(0.6deg * sin(2*PI*(ms-400)/5000)) about its root (trailing 0.4 s). UNLIT bays: unlit colours, no halo, no ghost, sway only.
DAY-1 PROOF: render 10 s and pull frames at 0, 2.5, 5, 7.5 s; it must read as a lantern turning. Fallback A: sway only (no torsion). Fallback B (owner's call on the flower): a four-petal jaali cut in the window instead of the I-flower, same motion, one-file swap. The kandil is never a joke in copy and never sits beside the wordmark (end cards carry no kandil).

system.recurring_devices:
C-WORLD (work/v3/world/world.html): one HTML scene 3258 x 5787 px plus 300 px of sky above (y -300..0) and 300 px of street below (y 5787..6087). Twelve 1080x1440 bays at x = (col-1)*1089, y = (row-1)*1449 with 9 px mortar joints. Bay origins: r1c1 P12 (0,0) · r1c2 P11 (1089,0) · r1c3 P10 (2178,0) · r2c1 P9 (0,1449) · r2c2 P8 (1089,1449) · r2c3 P7 (2178,1449) · r3c1 P6 (0,2898) · r3c2 P5 (1089,2898) · r3c3 P4 (2178,2898) · r4c1 P3 (0,4347) · r4c2 P2 (1089,4347) · r4c3 P1 (2178,4347). Each bay is a component (work/v3/world/bays/pNN.js) with three states, CLOSED, OPENING(t) and LIT (P5 also has DAY for its own cover and NIGHT-LIT for later establishing frames). Every reel, reel cover, carousel slide 1 and establishing frame is a camera on this file. A carousel slide 1 = the bay at scale 1 in a 1080x1440 viewport (translate(-bay.x, -bay.y)). A reel cover = the bay at scale 1 in 1080x1920 (translate(-bay.x, 240-bay.y)); its 240 px bands above and below show the neighbours in their state on the posting day under a plaster-tone veil (the storey colour at 45%), with any neighbour plate or fascia wordmark masked out, so the 9:16 cover carries exactly one mark.

C-CAMERA (work/v3/kit/camera.js, run in window.atTime): s0 = 1080/3258 = 0.331492; focal P = bay origin + (540,720). For progress e (eased by cubic-bezier(.65,0,.35,1) of time): s = s0 * (1/s0)^e; F = lerp(P*s0 + (0, 0.82), (540, 960), e) on reels; transform = translate(F - s*P) scale(s) with transform-origin 0 0. e = 0 is the establishing frame (the building exactly fills 1080 x 1920, 0.82 px letterbox), e = 1 is the cover framing. Push-ins beyond scale 1 never take a cut-out past its native resolution.

C-BOX, the real blush drawer box (work/v3/kit/box.js), ONE render path: a fixed 2D parallel projection of the box drawn as SVG faces (no three.js, no CSS preserve-3d, so nothing can mis-sort). Proportions from the site's NairaBoxCSS.tsx (W = D = 1.6, H = 0.7 units), assumed 95 x 95 x 42 mm until a real box is measured on day 1. Pose: yaw -28 deg, pitch 35 deg from above (the props' angle). Projection: X = cx + k*(x*cos(yaw) - y*sin(yaw)); Y = cy + k*((x*sin(yaw) + y*cos(yaw))*sin(pitch) - z*cos(pitch)); x runs along the drawer (toward the viewer's left), z up. Faces and colours from src/lib/nairaBox/config.ts: lid #F2DED8 -> #E6CCC5 -> #DDBFB8 (140 deg), visible side #C8A69F -> #B9968F, drawer front #F6D8D0 with the ribbon pull tab #E9C2BA (1 px #F6E2DC highlight), rim #E8D2CB (1 px light on every open edge), velvet bed radial #2E2527 -> #141112; every face multiplied with AP-02 at .40; soft contact shadow ellipse (multiply 30%). The lid print kit/motifs/box/naira-box-print.webp (#4A4440 at .86, 62% of lid width) is mapped onto the lid by the lid's affine matrix(). Drawer travel d (0 to 0.9 D) along +x with REVEAL timings (out 1.1 s cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1), home 1.0 s cubic-bezier(.65,0,.35,1)). Draw order: shadow, sleeve interior (dark), drawer group [velvet floor, far wall, THE PIECE, near side wall, front panel, pull tab], then the sleeve's lid and visible side face, so the drawer's inside part is hidden by construction. Velvet visible on any cover <= 3% of the tile (count dark pixels in QA). Proof frames at drawer 0, 50 and 100%. Drawer-end mini boxes (P1 shelf, P3 shelf) show only the end face and pull tab.

C-STRAND, string lights and wedding strands (work/v3/kit/strand.js): a strand is two SVG paths on the same curve: bulbs = stroke-width 7 (wedding) or 10 (terrace wire), stroke-dasharray '0 24' (or '0 54'), stroke-linecap round, colour #FFD9A0 / #FFF1DC, so the dash pattern IS the row of bulbs; glow = the same path at 2x width, filter blur(4px), 50% opacity, screen. Unfurl = clip-path inset(0 0 100% 0) -> inset(0) on the strand group; breathing = a travelling opacity wave on a 5.0 s period. posts.concept:
After 79 silent days the grid comes back the way every Indian shop comes back. The reel opens on the whole building at dusk, twelve dark bays and twelve unlit kandils, which is the exact shape of the profile grid. The camera finds Shop 1 on the ground floor, under a sage fascia carrying the real wordmark; the shutter rolls up into its drum; inside, in the dark, the bracelet is only its own traced outline; the tube light blinks twice and settles, and the outline develops into the photograph. On the blush velvet tray stands the oldest tent card in Indian retail, BACK IN 5 MINUTES, with the ruby Baguette Tennis Bracelet in front of it. The turn owns the gap honestly: 'eleven weeks, actually. new stock came in.' (Edition Two came in on 16 Oct.) The camera pulls back to a building with one window lit, and the season has its rule: one window a post.

posts.concept:
When an Indian building has a wedding, the building gets dressed: the lighting-wala hangs curtains of fairy lights from the terrace to the gate. On the last Sunday that is the reel: from the crown and the terrace coping, strands of warm light unfurl down the whole facade, over every window the season has lit (bulb 9 on 101's balcony still out under them), until the finished building, all twelve bays, glows. Then the crown lights: the real wordmark on its sage name panel, the brand's name at the top-left of the grid. On the parapet below it, on a fold of blush silk, lies the guests' set: the Baguette Tennis Necklace with its length falling over the coping like one more strand, the bracelet and the huggies, all in green. The camera pulls back to the whole building, which is now the whole profile, and the season ends on its thesis: the lights come down. the pieces stay.

EVERY WORD ON SCREEN: crown: the kit wordmark alone; 'EVEN THE' / 'BUILDING' / 'DRESSED UP.'; 'every flat is invited.' / 'the guests wear green.'; end card 'TERRACE · THE CROWN' / 'THE GREEN SET' / 'BAGUETTE TENNIS NECKLACE · ₹2,300' / 'BAGUETTE TENNIS BRACELET · ₹1,699' / 'BAGUETTE HUGGIES · ₹1,199' / '[ green cubic zirconia · 18k gold tone plated ]' / 'nairaflore.com' / 'the lights come down. the pieces stay.' / 'every piece arrives in our blush box · free insured shipping · COD available'.
